title: pvNormalGlyphs
body:
## pvNormalGlyphs

ParaView's compound Normal Glyphs filter: extracts the outer surface, computes one normal per surface cell, and draws an arrow glyph at every cell centre along that normal. The output is polydata of arrows, typically rendered over the surface to check normal orientation, e.g. before extrusion, offsets or boundary-condition assignment. Arrow length is the glyph scale factor in dataset units; all arrows have the same size.

Common mistakes and assumptions:

- Polygon ordering is used as found (Consistency is off in this filter by default), so mixed-orientation surfaces show arrows pointing both ways; that is often what you want to detect.
- Every surface cell gets an arrow; on large surfaces decimate or extract a region first.
- Schemaxis generates this binding from ParaView's catalogue; it has not run a native acceptance check for this operation.

Native constructor: `NormalGlyphs`. Identity: `filters/NormalGlyphs`. Role: `pipeline`. Output kinds: `["data"]`.

### Inputs

| Port | Meaning / native port | Required | Multiplicity | Kind | Contract |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `Input` | Required data input for the native Input port. Give the name of the upstream node to connect, or a {node, port} object to use another of its output ports. | True | one object | `data` | `{"compatibility":"native-domain-checked","composite":null,"cost":{"basis":"no benchmark","conversion":"none inserted","rating":"unknown"},"nativeTypes":[],"requirements":{},"traits":{"contiguity":"unknown","indexing":"unknown","iteration":"unknown"}}` |

### Options

| Key | Meaning / native assignment | Type and constraints | Default / required | Example value |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `Consistency` | The value of this property controls whether consistent polygon ordering is enforced. Generally the normals for a data set should either all point inward or all point outward. If the value of this property is 1, then this filter will reorder the points of cells that whose normal vectors are oriented the opposite direction from the rest of those in the data set. | `{"type":"boolean"}` | `native initialisation / omitted` | `false` |
| `GlyphMaxPoints` | Native Glyph MaximumNumberOfSamplePoints, which caps the number of glyphs only in the Glyph filter's uniform-spatial-distribution modes. Normal Glyphs fixes its internal glyph mode to All Points, so this value does not limit the arrows here. | `{"type":"integer"}` | `native initialisation / omitted` | `1` |
| `GlyphScaleFactor` | Length of every arrow in dataset coordinate units: the arrow source has unit length and no data array scales it, so this value is the displayed arrow length. Choose a few percent of the model size so arrows are visible without hiding the surface. | `{"type":"number"}` | `native initialisation / omitted` | `1` |
| `InvertArrow` | Reverses the arrow geometry so each glyph points against the computed normal instead of along it. Use it when the surface normals point into the body and you want arrows outside; the normals themselves are unchanged. | `{"type":"boolean"}` | `native initialisation / omitted` | `false` |

Execution contract:

```json
{
  "mode": "serial",
  "performance": "unknown"
}
```

Coverage and unbound native properties:

```json
{
  "defaults": "native defaults for omitted options",
  "gaps": {},
  "origin": "generated",
  "output": "native inspection required; explicit output-port selection available",
  "outputPorts": 1,
  "qualification": "not-run"

```

### Syntax example

Place in `nodes`. Data outputs may be selected by a scene; resource outputs must be connected to a compatible consumer.

```json
{
  "id": "result",
  "filter": "pvNormalGlyphs",
  "inputs": {
    "Input": "UPSTREAM_Input"
  }
}
```
